title: Casper and the Choir
premise: Freya Pemberton has spent her whole life as gatekeeper of the Hollow Gate, the one seam between the magicless valley of Vell and the vanished kingdom of Casper, which supposedly ceased to exist a century ago. When the crown's Inquisitors begin hunting the gifted and her valley's protection fails, Freya discovers the gate is dying—and that she is the last living key to the kingdom everyone believes is gone. Guided by a fugitive choir-master named Aldric, whose songs can open what swords cannot, she journeys through a country that exists only in memory and song, pursued by the Inquisitor who was once her mother's friend. At the climax Freya must choose between sealing the gate forever to save her valley or opening it to restore Casper, knowing the crown will burn whatever remains; she opens it only halfway, letting the kingdom's people pour into the world while the old magic dissolves, and she and Aldric remain as the new keepers of a door that is now just a door.
about_author: Xanthe Eriksen is the pen name of a former church organist from coastal Norway who writes fantasy about music, borders, and the people who guard them. Her short fiction has appeared in several small-press anthologies, and Casper and the Choir is her first novel.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She tends the Hollow Gate's moss-covered arch, performing rituals she half-believes in, while the valley below lives in deliberate ignorance of magic. A stray note of song makes the gate hum for the first time in years. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine, the sense that her careful life is balanced on something old and tired.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Mill
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A crown herald reads the Edict of Cleansing: all gifted persons must be surrendered. The villagers glance at Freya's family with new, calculating eyes. Her grandmother burns letters in the hearth. Emotional beat: the shattering of safety; invisibility revealed as an illusion everyone agreed to keep.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Buried
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Dying, her grandmother confesses: the valley's magiclessness is a ward, and the ward is anchored to Freya's bloodline—and it is failing. She gives Freya a tuning fork of white iron. Emotional beat: grief braided with betrayal; the inheritance Freya never wanted arrives anyway.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sang Through Locks
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Introduce Aldric, a choir-master smuggled out of the capital, whose voice can unmake wards. He is fleeing toward the valley, hunted by Inquisitor Serane Voss, who once sang beside him in the royal choir. Emotional beat: weary resolve; a man carrying a country in his throat.

chapters.title: Serane Voss
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. The Inquisitor interrogates a gifted child with terrible gentleness, believing mercy and duty are the same thing. She learns the last Pemberton still lives at the gate. Emotional beat: chilling conviction; the antagonist who thinks she is the story's conscience.

chapters.title: Soldiers at the Door
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Inquisitors reach the valley. Freya's neighbor betrays her; she flees through the gate as it cracks open for the first time in a century, stepping into a twilight country that should not exist. Emotional beat: terror and vertigo—the door out of a country that no longer exists, and it works.

chapters.title: The Country of Aftermath
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Inside the gate lies Casper: a kingdom frozen mid-sorrow, streets of memory where the dead repeat their last days. Freya meets the ghost-choir who sustain it. Emotional beat: haunted wonder; beauty and wrongness in equal measure.

chapters.title: Aldric in the Ash Choir
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. He reaches the gate and finds it empty, follows Freya's traces into Casper, and finds her cornered by memory-wraiths. He sings them still. They recognize each other: he knew her mother. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two orphans of different disasters.

chapters.title: The Choir's Bargain
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The ghost-choir reveals the truth: Casper was sealed away to save it from the crown's first purge, and it is starving. Only a living key can open the way out—but opening it will unmake the valley's ward, exposing everyone Freya left behind. Emotional beat: the weight of impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Lessons in the Drowned Cathedral
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Aldric begins teaching Freya the gate-songs, and she is terrible at first, then startlingly not. Growing warmth between them, undercut by the knowledge that one of them may have to die for the door. Emotional beat: tenderness as risk.

chapters.title: Serane Crosses the Threshold
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Voss breaks the valley's outer ward and follows them into Casper, where the kingdom's memories begin to show her what the crown erased. She refuses to see it. Emotional beat: a conscience slamming its own doors.

chapters.title: The Market of Last Days
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. To find the inner door, Freya and Aldric trade memories to a memory-broker—a risk, since memories are what anchor a key. Freya sells her happiest day with her grandmother. Emotional beat: sacrifice as currency; what identity costs.

chapters.title: What Serane Sold
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Voss bargains with the same broker and accidentally buys back a memory the crown took from her: she was Casper-born, a choir-child smuggled out as an infant. Emotional beat: the ground of her certainty giving way; duty curdling into grief.

chapters.title: The Bridge of Nailed Songs
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The inner door lies beyond a chasm crossed only by sung harmony—two voices, exactly matched. Freya and Aldric cross it together, closer than either has ever been to anyone. Emotional beat: love declared in the only language the crossing allows.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Dead Country
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They reach the inner door and find it needs a life freely given to stay open. Serane arrives, sword drawn—and instead of striking, she tells them the crown's true plan: not to purge the gifted but to harvest the gate itself. Emotional beat: enemy turned uneasy witness; the stakes tripled.

chapters.title: The Crown's Engineers
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Crown artificers breach Casper behind her, chaining the gate with iron hymns. The kingdom begins to collapse street by street; the ghost-choir's voices fray. Emotional beat: horror of institutional cruelty; Serane's defection begins.

chapters.title: Riot in the Memory Streets
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya, Aldric, and Serane fight through the collapsing city to reach the choir, Freya using the gate-songs as weapons for the first time. Aldric is gravely wounded shielding the last singers. Emotional beat: desperation; love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The choir offers Freya the choice: give her life to open the door fully, or seal it and save only herself. Aldric, dying, offers his instead. Freya refuses both—and realizes the door was never meant to take a life, only a name freely surrendered. Emotional beat: the riddle breaking open; defiance of every offered sacrifice.

chapters.title: Freya Pemberton, Given
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the gate's heart, Freya surrenders her name—not her life—unbinding herself from the valley and the crown's registers alike. The door opens. The people of Casper begin to pour through into the waking world. Emotional beat: transcendence through relinquishment; she becomes no one in order to become the way.

chapters.title: The Unmaking of the Kingdom
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. As Casper empties, its magic dissolves into the world, and the crown's engineers are unmade by the hymns they chained. Serane stands down her own soldiers, choosing exile over orders. Emotional beat: the cost of the crown's corruption paid in full; a defection completed.

chapters.title: A Door That Is Only a Door
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Casper is gone; the valley is free and frightened and beginning, tentatively, to sing. Aldric survives, voice scarred but whole. Freya, nameless on paper but not to him, takes up the gatekeeper's post one last time—and then leaves it open. Emotional beat: belonging found not in walls but in the choice to keep a way open.

chapters.title: Coda: The Choir Remembers
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. A year later: a village festival where Casper's songs and the valley's are sung as one; a white iron tuning fork hung above a plain wooden door; a child asks Freya her name and she says she is still deciding. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope; the theme of belonging resolved in community rather than blood or crown.
